schema_note: The deployed system has 3 risk levels (LOW/MODERATE/HIGH); CRITICAL was retired pre-v1.1.0 and now surfaces as HIGH + an 'urgent' priority flag (composite >= 0.70). All headline figures below (accuracy, macro_f1, weighted_f1, high_recall) are computed on that 3-class deployed schema -- i.e. with the notebook's raw 4-class CRITICAL row/column folded into HIGH on both axes, exactly as inference_service.py folds them at inference time. The unfolded 4-class notebook sanity check (rule-based risk_level_rule vs GBR/RFR ensemble, informative but not the deployed schema) is kept below as classification_report_4class_notebook_raw for transparency. See docs/model-validation-defensible-statements.md Part 3 for why CRITICAL was retired.

classification_report_4class_notebook_ra.note: Raw notebook cell-52 output before folding CRITICAL into HIGH. The macro avg here (0.5686) is depressed by a CRITICAL class with 0 support -- it is not a defensible headline number and should not be quoted as 'the' macro-F1. Use classification_report_3class.macro avg (0.7740) instead.

decision_support_note: Risk levels are decision-support indicators, not clinical diagnoses. CRITICAL (composite >= 0.70) triggers priority referral and immediate case management review. HIGH predicted as CRITICAL (or vice versa) counts as a successful priority flag in the priority_capture_rate metric -- which is also why, once folded into the deployed 3-class schema, high_recall reaches 1.0 (19/19): every rule-flagged HIGH/CRITICAL senior is caught by the ensemble as HIGH or higher.
